name: Zinc
mobility: Partially mobile (deficiency mostly on YOUNGER-to-MIDDLE leaves; interveinal + short internodes)

overview.whyImportant: Zinc is the MOST widespread micronutrient deficiency in Indian soils (esp. rice-wheat belt). It is vital for auxin (growth hormone) synthesis, enzyme systems and protein metabolism. Deficiency causes stunting, short internodes, and interveinal chlorosis — 'khaira' in rice.

plantFunctions.roleInsidePlant: Enzyme cofactor (carbonic anhydrase, dehydrogenases), auxin (IAA) synthesis, protein metabolism.
plantFunctions.vegetativeGrowth: Drives internode elongation — deficiency gives rosetting/short internodes.
plantFunctions.proteinSynthesis: Needed for ribosome integrity and protein synthesis.
plantFunctions.yieldContribution: Large in rice/wheat/maize/citrus; deficiency sharply cuts yield.

whyDeficiencyHappens.why: Zn forms insoluble compounds above pH 7 — main cause.
Usually adequate; leaching in very acid sandy soils.
Reduced soil chemistry ties up Zn; bicarbonate build-up.
High P strongly induces Zn deficiency (P-Zn antagonism) — classic in over-DAP fields.
Forms insoluble zinc phosphate and dilutes Zn in fast-growing tissue.
Growth dilution can trigger Zn shortfall.
Not applying ZnSO4 in rice-wheat; over-P; ignoring soil tests.

symptoms.note: Deficiency mostly on younger-to-middle leaves; interveinal chlorosis + SHORT INTERNODES (rosetting) and small leaves.
symptoms.early: Middle/young leaves interveinal yellowing; slightly reduced growth.
symptoms.middle: Interveinal chlorosis, bronzing (rice khaira), small leaves, shortened internodes (rosetting).
symptoms.severe: Stunted rosetted plant, brown-bronze necrotic patches, poor tillering/branching, delayed maturity.
symptoms.oldLeaves: May show some chlorosis but classic sign is middle/young leaves + rosetting.
symptoms.seed: Low set and Zn content in grain (nutritional concern).
symptoms.wholePlant: Stunted rosetted plant with interveinal chlorosis/bronzing and short internodes — the khaira/little-leaf picture.

cropWiseSymptoms.symptoms: KHAIRA — bronze/rusty spots on lower-mid leaves 2-3 weeks after transplant, stunting, delayed tillering; worst in flooded calcareous soils.
Interveinal chlorosis of middle leaves, short internodes, small leaves.
Interveinal chlorosis, small leaves, stunting on calcareous soils.
Small young leaves, interveinal chlorosis, short internodes (little-leaf).
Little-leaf, interveinal chlorosis in high-P/high-pH conditions.
Small chlorotic young leaves, stunted rosette.
Small mottled young leaves, short internodes, poor fruit set.
Small interveinal-chlorotic young leaves, short internodes.
Broad white/yellow interveinal band on younger leaves (white bud), short internodes, stunting — highly Zn-responsive.
Interveinal chlorosis, stunting on sandy calcareous soils.
Interveinal chlorosis of middle leaves, short internodes.
Interveinal chlorosis/white streaks on younger leaves, short internodes, thin canes.

howToFix.bestCropStage: Basal at sowing/transplant; foliar on symptoms
howToFix.methodOfApplication: Soil basal (residual for 2-3 crops) or foliar for quick fix
howToFix.precautions: Add lime to foliar ZnSO4 to prevent leaf scorch; don't band with P.

howToFix.methodOfApplication: Soil/foliar; higher Zn concentration than hepta form

howToFix.precautions: Common rice practice — dip seedling roots in 2% ZnO suspension.

methodOfApplication.broadcast: ZnSO4 broadcast + incorporate basal — residual benefit 2-3 crops.
methodOfApplication.bandPlacement: Band ZnSO4, but NOT with P fertiliser (they react).
methodOfApplication.foliarSpray: 0.5% ZnSO4 + 0.25% lime for quick correction; repeat.
methodOfApplication.rootDrench: Rice seedling-root dip in ZnO suspension.
methodOfApplication.seedTreatment: ZnO seed coating in cereals on deficient soils.

toxicity.whatHappens: Zn toxicity is rare; occurs near industrial/contaminated soils or huge over-application.
toxicity.plantToxicitySymptoms: Induced iron deficiency (young-leaf chlorosis), stunted roots, brown root tips.
toxicity.yieldLoss: Via induced Fe deficiency and root damage.
toxicity.correctionMethods: Stop Zn; apply Fe; lime acid contaminated soils to reduce Zn availability.

prevention: Apply ZnSO4 10 kg/acre basal every 2-3 seasons in rice-wheat and Zn-deficient soils.
Avoid over-P which induces Zn deficiency.
Use Zn seed treatment/seedling dip in rice.
Build organic matter for Zn cycling.
Foliar Zn preventively in maize/rice on deficient soils.
Balance N so growth doesn't dilute Zn.
commonFarmerMistakes: Ignoring Zn in the rice-wheat system — the most widespread deficiency.
Over-applying DAP/P and inducing Zn deficiency.
Banding Zn together with phosphate (they react, both lost).
Confusing Zn (short internodes/rosette) with Fe/Mn chlorosis.
Foliar ZnSO4 without lime, causing leaf scorch.
Not doing rice seedling-root Zn dip.
Assuming one Zn application lasts forever (reapply every 2-3 crops).
Skipping soil test for available Zn.
Not correcting the P excess behind the deficiency.
Over-applying Zn near contaminated soils (Fe lock-up).

New/middle leaves respond — judge success there.
Avoid over-liming on Zn-marginal soils.

faq.q: Dhaan me khaira (bronze dhabbe) kya hai?
faq.a: Zinc ki kami — transplant ke 2-3 hafte baad neeche-madhya patti par bronze dhabbe. ZnSO4 10 kg/acre basal, ya seedling root ko 2% ZnO me dip karein.
Chhote internodes (rosette), chhoti patti + interveinal chlorosis/bronzing.

faq.q: Zn ko P ke saath band me de sakte hain?
faq.a: Nahi — Zn aur P react karke dono lock ho jate hain. Alag dein.
Leaf scorch se bachne ke liye 0.25% lime milayein.
Haan — zyada P Zn deficiency induce karta hai. P kam karein, Zn dein.
